_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description:
"The container" is the messages container (".messages-container"), "the button" the scroll-to-bottom button (".scroll-to-bottom-button"), and "the gap" the container's scrollHeight - clientHeight - scrollTop. To "send" a message, fill the message input ([data-testid="message-input"]) with it and click the send button ([data-testid="send-button"]). Check every assertion with an eval that has "expect" (or an assert_* or wait_* step): an eval without "expect" asserts nothing. When a step says to record something, do it in one eval without "expect" that stores it in the named window variable, then check that variable. Perform the steps in order. The test seeds a long conversation with ID {{ID}}; to "open the conversation", navigate to /c/{{ID}}, wait for the message input ([data-testid="message-input"]) to be visible (allow 30s), then wait for the first [data-testid="message"] element to be visible (allow 30s). "Scroll up" means: eval setting the container's scrollTop to 0; the button should become visible (allow 10s). "Still up" means: record the container's scrollTop in window.__top, then window.__top < 50 must be true. Focus matters here: press keys with press_key steps alone, and add no clicks the steps do not ask for. Cmd/Ctrl+ArrowDown leaves the caret alone when the composer has text below it.
1. Open the conversation.
2. Fill the message input with "first line\nsecond line" (two lines). Eval setting its selectionStart and selectionEnd to 0.
3. Scroll up.
4. Press ArrowDown with the Control modifier.
5. Wait until the message input's selectionEnd >= 11 is true (allow 5s): the caret left the first line.
6. Still up.
